FESTIVALS & EVENTS

Editor's Pick: Open Monuments Day

Image from Kees Hummel

This weekend, you can visit 50 monuments during Open Monuments Day. Take a look inside the renovated Van Gendt Halls, where locomotives and marine engines were once built, or climb Amsterdam’s first skyscraper. There’s also plenty to do in the evening: from the roof of Felix Meritis, you can gaze at the stars. Fun fact: the dome of this listed building once housed one of Europe’s oldest astronomical observatories. These 12 monuments are well worth visiting.

Heritage Open Days | 12–13 September | throughout Amsterdam | Free

Read My World

Image from Rashif Oehlers

More than 60 writers, musicians and artists are gathering this weekend at the Tolhuistuin for the Read My World Festival. Listen to live music and readings, visit the book market or go to a performance or talk. This year’s theme is Oceanic Solidarity, highlighting the history and culture of Maluku, West Papua, the Caribbean and the Netherlands. One of the performances that ties in with this is Sounds of the Island: where five islanders tell stories about their lives through poetry and music. In the talk 'Speaking at a Cost', writer and columnist Dalilla Hermans, artist Gispa Ferdinanda Warijo, and writer, poet and spoken-word artist Asmae Amaddaou discuss activism, resistance and the cost of speaking out publicly.

Read My World | 11–12 September | 18:30–23:00 - 12:00–23:30 | Tolhuistuin | From €20

CLUBBING & PARTIES

Phono Lake Festival

Boutique techno along the lake at one of Amsterdam’s most picturesque venues? Few things sound better, so head to Phono Lake Festival for a gorgeous daytime dance in September. In collaboration with Breakfast Club, this a celebration of house music, where lake and forest meet. It’s already selling out, but the official resale is up.

12 September | 13:00-23:00 | Sloterplas

CONCERTS & GIGS

Pearls of the City

Fancy a weekend full of music? At Parels van de Stad at Riekerhaven, you can choose from 9 stages and more than 150 artists over 2 days. Hip-hop, R&B, Afro, house and pop are all on the bill, with artists including Jonna Fraser, Broederliefde, Yade Lauren and Monica Geuze taking to the stage. If you want to start the festival weekend in an active way, you can take part in the Parels Run, a 6-kilometre run through Amsterdam. That way, you’ll arrive at the festival site feeling fit. And that’s a nice bonus if you’re over 20 by now.

Pearls of the City | 12–13 September | 12:00–23:00 - 13:00–23:00 | Riekerhaven | From €40.00

Side to Side

For those who prefer an intimate musical evening with DJs playing right among the crowd, there’s Side to Side, a new dance event by Zijkant. The first edition will take place in Amsterdam’s Houthavens. No huge main stage or DJs towering above the crowd, but a small-scale setting where you experience the music up close. Expect UK Garage, Deep House, Tech House and Minimal, with Melle & Melle, Bram and Jens behind the decks.

Side to Side | 12 September | 22:00–04:00 | The Other Side | From €12.50

Open House X TF at Meervaart

Looking for a fun family day out? During Open House X TF at Meervaart, children can take part in creative workshops for free. From ballet and street dance classes to making music and acting: there’s plenty to choose from. Prefer an afternoon of theatre? Then join us for Sam & Julia or Dag Poes. You can also take part in a backstage tour of the Blue and Red Halls, where you’ll discover how a production comes together.

Open House X TF at Meervaart | 12 September | 12:00 - 17:00 | Meervaart | Free

EAT & DRINK

Cinema Culinair: film and brunch

Going to the cinema is fun, but what if you could eat exactly the same food as in the film? You can at Cinema Culinair. This pop-up cinema takes place at the Tolhuistheater, where you can sit down for, among others, The Grand Budapest Hotel and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. Expect something elegant on your plate for the former, and mostly chocolate and other sweet treats for the latter (Willy Wonka wouldn’t have it any other way). The film Ratatouille is also on the programme. And let’s be honest: when you see Remy cooking up a storm on screen, you naturally don’t want to be sitting there with a tub of popcorn in front of you.

Cinema Culinair | varying dates | Het Tolhuis | From €89.95

Kwaku Downtown

If you want to squeeze a little more summer into your diary, head to the Vondelpark on Sunday. Kwaku Downtown is bringing those familiar Kwaku vibes to the Open-Air Theatre, with music and, most importantly, (lots of!) Surinamese food. Think fresh roti, crispy bara, moksi and shaved ice. On stage, Nikia Saunders, Massiv’ Live Band and Tranga Rugie will be keeping the music going. You can dance those calories right back off.

Kwaku Downtown | Vondelpark | 13 September | 13:00 - 21:00 | Free

SHOPPING & MARKETS

Biennale Pakhuis Wilhelmina

If you’re already heading out this weekend for Open Monument Days, you can drop by Pakhuis Wilhelmina while you’re at it. During the third Biennial, artists and designers are opening their studios to the public. It’s a great opportunity to wander through the building and take a look at the workspaces of various creative makers. But there’s much more to do besides. There are exhibitions, workshops, a film screening and a pop-up shop. So put on your walking shoes, because there’s plenty to discover.

Biennale Pakhuis Wilhelmina | 12–13 September | 12:00–18:00 | Pakhuis Wilhelmina | Free

@ H'ART: Vintage Market

Anyone who loves rummaging through vintage treasures can indulge themselves (ha-ha) this Saturday at H’ART Museum’s vintage market. The courtyard will be filled with stalls packed with clothing, art and curiosities. In between shopping, you can get creative yourself during the upcycling workshop by Atelier Amsterdam Offline, where you’ll give a garment a new look with paint and stamps. Afterwards, you can enjoy a drink and live music from ska band De Stokers. 

@ H'ART: Vintage Market | 12 September | 12:00 - 17:00 | H'ART Museum | Free
